liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Slewfoot** (4 reviews, 1 other source): Slewfoot is described as a rare performance, opening a relaxed first half of newer material; Slewfoot was played only a handful of times; Garcia plays pedal steel on it [1][5][6][7][11]
- **Casey Jones** (3 reviews): Early Casey Jones comes with a very cool introduction; Very early Casey Jones with a long instrumental lead-in and slower, groovy jams in the middle [5][12][14]
- **Dire Wolf** (2 reviews, 1 other source): Dire Wolf features Garcia on pedal steel and Weir singing lead; Weir sings the vocals on Dire Wolf [2][12][14]
- **Sitting On Top of the World** (1 review): Double drumming comes back into its own once this song starts [10]
- **Big Boss Man** (1 review): Big Boss Man is played with real fire [10]
- **Green, Green Grass of Home** (1 review): The abrupt shift from the driving Eleven into country-flavored Green Green Grass of Home is striking [15]

## Setlist highlights

- **Slewfoot**: rare: 9 archived performances [17]
- **Big Boss Man**: back after 112 archived shows (663 days) [17]
- **Green, Green Grass of Home**: rare: 8 archived performances [17]

## The recordings

- **gd1969-06-27.166576.sbd.anon.gems.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 16 songs; 105 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd69-06-27.sbd.samaritano.20547.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 15 songs; 94 min; rated 4.1/5 by 20 [2]. Said about its sound: Overall sound quality is very good, better than the reviewer's own earlier cassette-derived copy; Sound is good, but the reviewer finds their own cassette fuller and equally crisp; Sounds quite good for its age, apart from some uneven mixing in part of Slewfoot [5][6][7][8][10]
- **gd1969-06-27.sbd.finney.10344.shnf**: soundboard; 14 songs; 88 min; rated 3.4/5 by 5 [4]. Said about its sound: The original Slewfoot recording apparently had its levels set too high at the start [4]
- **gd69-06-27.sbd.finney.78.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 14 songs; 93 min; rated 3.5/5 by 4 [3]

## Around the show

- The band was introduced from the stage as coming from San Francisco [6]
- Peter Grant played banjo on Slewfoot [2]
- The band is introduced as the good old Grateful Dead from San Francisco [4]
- This early Casey Jones rocks differently from the faster, familiar versions of later years [12]
- This early Casey Jones rocks differently from the faster, familiar versions of later years [14]
- This is among the earliest circulating versions of Casey Jones [13]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1969-06-27.166576.sbd.anon.gems.flac16**: taped by Anon; transferred by Mastering by Jim Blackwood Speed/pitch adjusted by Jason Chastain Minor repairs, track, FLAC, and pack by Steve Gravel; source: SBD master reel > DAT > AIFF [1]
- **gd69-06-27.sbd.samaritano.20547.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Joe Samaritano; source: Soundboard (no DAE) [2]
- **gd1969-06-27.sbd.finney.10344.shnf**: transferred by DFinnney and CPelz; source: SBD > Master Reel [4]. Also: Digitized from a cassette copy of the show [4]
- **gd69-06-27.sbd.finney.78.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by David Finney; source: Soundboard [3]
- Source is soundboard to master reel; a glitch occurs around 4:23 on disc 1 track 7 [20]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Veterans Auditorium - June 27, 1969](https://www.dead.net/show/june-27-1969) [22]
- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Veterans Auditorium, Santa Rosa Poster](https://www.dead.net/archives/1969/artwork/veterans-auditorium-santa-rosa-poster) [23]
- Fan art by LiveGRATEFUL.net: [Grateful Dead 1969-06-27 Fri Veterans Memorial Auditorium, Santa Rosa, CA](https://www.livegrateful.net/post/1389837363372/grateful-dead-1969-06-27-fri-veterans) [24]
